clue.text: One's expired, having died out of reach

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it, so the letter for died leaves the synonym for reach

parts.note: reach means breadth, extent

explanation.surface: Someone has breathed their last after drifting beyond help.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath is air that is expired, i.e. breathed out, so it is one thing expired.

clue.text: Fruity work of 23 10

definitions.meaning: fruity is slang for mad or crazy, as is the slang word for a yellow fruit
a 1971 comedy film directed by and starring the director at 23/10

explanation.surface: A fruit-filled piece by the director named in another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both crazy (informal) and the title of an early film by that director.

clue.text: On which our existence is terminal

definitions.meaning: an electrical ... connection is a terminal in a circuit

explanation.surface: A gloomy thought that life is fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is where we exist; in electrics a ground connection, an earth terminal.

clue.text: Doctor cries for author and people in work of 23 10

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic shouts for a writer and a crowd during a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal; CRIESFORAUTHOR plus PEOPLE rearranges to the 1985 film title, entered across 3, 17 and 26.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1985 film written and directed by the director at 23/10.

clue.text: Was catty, as 23 10 in arrears with child maintenance?

definitions.meaning: made the cry of a cat

definitions.text: as 23 10 in arrears with child maintenance?
definitions.meaning: the director's former partner was Mia Farrow, so if he were behind on payments, Mia would be owed

explanation.surface: A spiteful remark from a filmmaker behind on support payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat mews, so making that noise is being literally catty; split, it says Mia was owed.

clue.text: Philosopher not entirely wet, though one raises the water level

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

indicators.note: not entirely means the synonym for wet loses its final letter

parts.note: wet means damp

explanation.surface: A thinker who is a bit damp, yet raises things.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier across a stream that holds water back to drive a mill raises the water level behind it.

clue.text: It's memorable, though somewhat short of fashionable

indicators.note: somewhat short of means the phrase for fashionable is cut down at its end

parts.note: a la mode means in fashion

explanation.surface: Something unforgettable that falls a little short of being trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remember the Alamo!' was the Texan battle cry after the 1836 siege, hence 'memorable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan mission is famously to be remembered, from the rallying cry 'Remember the Alamo'.

clue.text: Wimp about to ring up model, performed admirably

indicators.note: about means going round, so the synonym for wimp surrounds the rest

parts.note: a weed is a feeble person, a wimp

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T

explanation.surface: A weakling phones a fashion model and gives a fine performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wimp' looks like the definition but is the outer piece; the Model T convention gives T, and 'up' suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-acted was performed with skill, admirably.

clue.text: European ruin involves six counties

indicators.note: involves means the word for ruin wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: to dash hopes is to ruin them
Northern Ireland is made up of six counties, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A European's ruin takes in six counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland, part of the UK, consists of six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane, someone from Denmark, is a European; the adjective names him as such.

clue.text: Tail of largest howler monkey

indicators.note: tail of means the last letter of the word largest

parts.note: a howler is a glaring mistake, an error

explanation.surface: The tail of the biggest howler monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'howler monkey' is a real animal, but split: the howler is a mistake, and 'monkey' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little monkey or a little terror, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Face report of trade, sensational thing

parts.note: to face something is to brave it, to nerve oneself; face also means cheek or nerve

indicators.note: report of means a word heard spoken, here the one for trade

parts.note: to trade is to sell

explanation.surface: Confronting news of commerce, a sensational item.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron carries sensation through the body, so it is literally a thing of sensation.

clue.text: See 23
Run off to abduct what? The Indian PM

indicators.note: to abduct means to take in and hold, so the shuffled word holds the exclamation
off means the letters of run are thrown out of order

parts.note: eh? is a query meaning what?

explanation.surface: A man flees to kidnap someone, and the Indian Prime Minister is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what?' as a query giving EH is a common crossword device; 'off' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister.

clue.text: A semiconductor almost breaking paths of light in work of 23 10

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the word for light paths, with the rest inside

parts.note: rays are paths of light

indicators.note: almost means the word for the semiconductor loses its last letter

parts.note: a diode is a semiconductor device

explanation.surface: An electronic component breaks up beams in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paths of light' is the container, not the definition; the film title is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1987 film by the director at 23/10, about radio in his childhood.

clue.text: Work of 23 10 run over by a train?

definitions.meaning: a 1973 science-fiction comedy by the director
a railway tie, the timber beneath the rails over which trains run

explanation.surface: A film that ends with someone flattened on the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is the British name for a railway tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a 1973 film by the director and the beam a train runs over.

clue.text: Bringing to mind end of message, then calling

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word message

parts.note: a calling is a vocation

explanation.surface: Recollection comes at the close of a message, then a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Evoking a memory is bringing it to mind; the noun names that act.

clue.text: Work of 23 10 could bark: time to die barking

parts.note: might means could
to yap is to bark
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a time

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film that might bark, before it's time to die raving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (British for crazy) shuffles HR plus TODIE into HRODITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1995 film by the director at 23/10, across 15 and 27.

clue.text: Pompous relative dies, unfortunately without love

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the shuffled letters surround the zero
unfortunately means the letters of dies come out badly ordered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A relative passes away sadly, unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges DIES to DISE, and 'without' (outside) puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose and pompous both describe something showy and self-important.

clue.text: See 3
Having depression, though not quite finished in destiny

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word sits inside the word for destiny

parts.note: fate means destiny

indicators.note: not quite means the word for finished loses its last letter

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: Feeling low, though destiny's work isn't done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims OVER to OVE, placed in FATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, foveate means pitted, having a small depression or fovea.

clue.text: When this full, head for bathroom — run!

definitions.text: When this full, head for bathroom — run!

indicators.note: head for means the first letter of bathroom

parts.note: a ladder is a run in tights

explanation.surface: Advice to dash for the loo when the need arises.
explanation.walkthrough: A run in stockings is called a ladder in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A full bladder sends one to the bathroom at a run, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Big girl out of 1 across

indicators.note: out of means made from rearranging those letters

parts.note: the solution at 1 across, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A large girl made from the answer to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was the nickname of a huge German First World War gun.

clue.text: Sound advice for boating companion, graceful thing

indicators.note: sound means the words are heard spoken

parts.note: telling a companion in a boat 'row, dear'

explanation.surface: Sensible tips for a fellow rower, said gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A small deer, a graceful animal.

clue.text: Waste material, high percentage

parts.note: high meat has gone off
a cut is a share or percentage

explanation.surface: Rubbish yields a large share.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover scrap trimmed from timber or cloth, waste material.

clue.text: Government leader trapped by failing to declare patriot

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the word for failing

parts.note: a failing is a flaw

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Government

parts.note: to aver is to declare

explanation.surface: A political leader caught out failing to declare himself a patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot enthusiastically waves the national flag.

clue.text: Director of some yarn about day at sea

indicators.note: about means the word for yarn-made goes round the rest

parts.note: woollen means made of wool, a type of yarn

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of day are rearranged

explanation.surface: A filmmaker tells a tale about a day spent on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some yarn' looks like a tale, but 'of some yarn' describes material made from wool; 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen is an American film director.

clue.text: Flier and sailor

definitions.meaning: a male duck, a bird that flies

explanation.surface: An airman and a seaman together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a male duck and the famous English navigator.

clue.text: A bunch of crawlers in work of 23 10

parts.note: lice are small crawling insects

explanation.surface: Creepy-crawlies infest a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1990 film by the director at 23/10.

clue.text: See 3
See 15
Can order photo

parts.note: a tin is a can
an order is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Someone can request a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is an early photograph on a thin iron plate.

clue.text: Measure, or bright streak

parts.note: to mete is to measure out

explanation.surface: A measure or a bright line.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a shooting star, seen as a bright streak in the sky.
